title: Earlier Lifeline for Rural Hospitals Faces Test Under ‘Big Beautiful’ Law
summary: A century-old rural Michigan hospital converted to a stripped-down model Congress created to help keep small facilities afloat, then it closed. The emergency hospital model, created a few years ago, is stabilizing some hospitals, arrived too late for others, and now faces major challenges under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

title: Kennedy, Oz Contend Fraud Crackdown, Not Skyrocketing Prices, Led Millions To Leave Obamacare
summary: Rising premiums forced many people in Affordable Care Act plans to give up their coverage. But the Trump administration claims a huge drop in enrollment is almost entirely due to its fraud crackdown.

title: People With Disabilities Fear Service Cuts as Trump’s DOJ Questions Legal Protections
summary: The Department of Justice in June issued a legal opinion saying states aren’t required to provide services that help people with disabilities remain in their homes. The new position has added momentum to states’ existing legal challenges to the requirement and triggered worries among people who rely on these services.

title: Journalists Catch You Up on Fauci Hearing, Peptides, and Kids’ Caffeine Consumption
summary: KFF Health News journalists made the rounds on national or local media recently to discuss topical stories. Here’s a collection of their appearances.

title: The Newest Federally Recognized Tribe Wants Better Healthcare. It May Be On Its Own.
summary: North Carolina's Robeson County, where most of the tribe’s citizens live, ranks as one of the worst counties in the U.S. for health disparities. After securing federal recognition, Lumbee tribal leaders will have to decide how to address them.

title: They Worked To Protect Public Health. Now They Want the Public’s Votes.
summary: They’re known for touting pandemic precautions, Affordable Care Act plans, and testing for lead in schools. This year, some former public health officials are touting themselves — for governor or senator.

title: Listen to the Latest ‘KFF Health News Minute’
summary: The "KFF Health News Minute" brings original healthcare and health policy reporting from our newsroom to the airwaves each week.

title: Abortion Drug Law in Louisiana Heightens Hemorrhage Risk for Pregnant Patients
summary: A 2024 state law reclassified misoprostol and mifepristone as controlled substances. That affects how hospitals can access the drugs in non-abortion emergencies, and other states appear to be taking note.

title: Medicaid Insurers’ Contracts on the Line in Tight Governor’s Race
summary: The Democratic candidate for governor says he would make Iowa the second state to drop private Medicaid management companies, which he calls “a disaster.”

title: Hospice’s Bad Reputation Amid Fraud Crisis Will Hurt Patients, Industry Experts Warn
summary: While acknowledging that changes must be made to the hospice industry, health policy researchers and providers worry that negative attention and the potential for overly punitive regulations could put patients at risk.
